text: No, not better. A pip package is just a Python wrapper around the same REST/websocket calls, and the app and engine are Kotlin, so they already talk to those APIs directly with our own rate gates, key rotation, usage meters and fallbacks. Adding Python wrappers would add a second runtime with none of that. I only use pip packages in the Python tools (data crunching), where they save time. If one of your APIs has a feature our Kotlin client lacks, tell me which and I'll add it natively.
